b2-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: So That Everyone Knows
b2-12-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you sent an email to the whole office. You sent it so that everyone would know the new time of the meeting.
b2-12-01.prompt: Tell Meg why you sent the email.
cues: Say that you sent the email
Say what you wanted everyone to know
b2-12-01.target: Mandé el correo a fin de que todos supieran la nueva hora de la reunión.
b2-12-01.english: I sent the email so that everyone would know the new time of the meeting.
b2-12-01.canDo: I can state a purpose with a fin de que and con el objeto de que and the right subjunctive tense.

b2-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: In Order To
b2-12-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you are going to the market. You are going to buy fruit and vegetables for dinner.
b2-12-02.prompt: Tell Carlos why you are going to the market.
cues: Say that you are going to the market
Say what you want to buy
b2-12-02.target: Voy al mercado a fin de comprar frutas y verduras para la cena.
b2-12-02.english: I am going to the market in order to buy fruit and vegetables for dinner.
b2-12-02.canDo: I can state a purpose with para, a fin de and con el objeto de + infinitive when one person acts.

b2-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: With a View To
b2-12-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you are saving money. You are saving it with a view to travelling next summer.
b2-12-03.prompt: Tell Meg why you are saving money.
cues: Say that you are saving money
Say what you are planning for next summer
b2-12-03.target: Ahorro dinero con miras a viajar el próximo verano.
b2-12-03.english: I am saving money with a view to travelling next summer.
b2-12-03.canDo: I can state a plan with con miras a and con vistas a + infinitive or noun.

b2-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Just in Case
b2-12-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is going out for a walk and the sky is grey. You tell him to take an umbrella in case it rains.
b2-12-04.prompt: Tell Carlos to take an umbrella and say why.
cues: Tell him to take an umbrella
b2-12-04.target: Lleva un paraguas, no sea que llueva.
b2-12-04.english: Take an umbrella, in case it rains.
b2-12-04.canDo: I can say what I want to avoid with para que no, a fin de que no and para no + infinitive.

b2-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Had More Time
b2-12-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you would do if you had more free time. You say that you would cook for her so that she could rest.
b2-12-05.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do with more free time and why.
cues: Say what you would do with more time
Say what you would do it for
b2-12-05.target: Si tuviera más tiempo libre, cocinaría para que tú descansaras.
b2-12-05.english: If I had more free time, I would cook so that you could rest.
b2-12-05.canDo: I can add a purpose clause to a hypothetical sentence with the imperfect subjunctive.

b2-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Before Opening the Book
b2-12-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you are reading about Ernesto Sabato. You want to know who he was before you open his novel El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos why you are reading about Sabato.
cues: Say that you are reading about Sabato
Say what you want to know before the novel
b2-12-consolidation.target: Leo sobre Sabato para saber quién fue antes de abrir El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.english: I am reading about Sabato to find out who he was before I open El túnel.
b2-12-consolidation.canDo: I can state a purpose with para, a fin de, con el objeto de and con miras a, with an infinitive or que + subjunctive.
